answer: active eq true and emails[type eq "work" and value ew "@example.com"]  -- the [ ] value filter makes type and the domain test apply to the SAME email (emails.type eq "work" and emails.value ew "..." could match two different emails). Booleans are bare lowercase (true), strings in double quotes; emails.value is caseExact false so ew is case-insensitive. URL-encode it in GET (?filter=active%20eq%20true%20and%20emails%5Btype%20eq%20%22work%22...), or send it in POST /Users/.search. Filtering is optional (ServiceProviderConfig filter.supported). Checker: OK.

PATCH /Groups/{id} with a remove whose path selects the member by a value filter: {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],"Operations":[{"op":"remove","path":"members[value eq \"2819c223-7f76-453a-919d-413861904646\"]"}]}. Do NOT send path "members" with a value array: RFC 7644 defines no value for remove, so a strict server removes ALL members; likewise replace on members replaces the whole membership. If the filter matches nothing the server returns 400 noTarget. Success is 200 with the group or 204 No Content. PATCH support is optional (ServiceProviderConfig patch.supported). Checker: OK.

Query parameters startIndex and count (RFC 7644 3.4.2.4); in POST /.search they are body fields. startIndex is 1-based (values < 1 are treated as 1); count is the requested page size (server may return fewer; count=0 returns only totalResults; negative treated as 0). In the ListResponse, totalResults is the total number of matches across all pages, itemsPerPage is the number of resources in this page, and startIndex echoes the 1-based index of the first returned result. Stop when startIndex + itemsPerPage > totalResults or a page is empty; index paging is not a snapshot, so results can shift if data changes.

No. Per RFC 7644 3.12 an error body must have "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:Error"], "status" must be the HTTP status as a JSON string ("400", not the number 400), and "invalidAttribute" is not a defined scimType; valid ones are invalidFilter, tooMany, uniqueness, mutability, invalidSyntax, invalidPath, noTarget, invalidValue, invalidVers, sensitive (for a bad attribute value use invalidValue; for an unknown attribute in a filter, invalidFilter). Compliant: {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:Error"],"status":"400","scimType":"invalidValue","detail":"..."}. Clients should still tolerate numeric status and missing scimType. Checker: original FAIL (3 errors), corrected OK.

employeeNumber is in the Enterprise User extension (urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User), a single-valued readWrite string, not a core User attribute. Put it inside an object keyed by the URN and list the URN in schemas: {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User","urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User"],"userName":"bjensen","urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User":{"employeeNumber":"701984"}}. Filter with the fully qualified path and a quoted string: urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User:employeeNumber eq "701984" (short "employeeNumber" works only if the server resolves it). Checker: OK.

409 Conflict with scimType "uniqueness" (RFC 7644 3.3), since userName has uniqueness: server. Body: {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:Error"],"status":"409","scimType":"uniqueness","detail":"userName already exists"}. Note Table 9 lists scimType values under 400, so some servers return 400 uniqueness; servers should follow 3.3 (409) and clients should handle both.

No: id and meta are readOnly and assigned by the server; a client must not send them on create (POST) and cannot change them (PUT keeps readOnly values; a PATCH on them fails with 400 mutability). Use externalId (or userName) for the client-side key. password is writeOnly with returned: never, so it is never returned in any response (GET, create, PUT, PATCH, list), even if requested via attributes=. Clients may set it (if the server supports it; changePassword in ServiceProviderConfig).

No to gt/lt/ge/le on booleans: ordering operators are not allowed on boolean (and binary) attributes and the server must return 400 invalidFilter; use active eq true / active eq false. emails co "example.com" without a sub-attribute: RFC 7644 3.4.2.2 requires a sub-attribute for complex attributes (emails.value co "example.com"), although the RFC's own examples use the short form and many servers read it as emails.value; for portability write emails.value co "example.com" or emails[value co "example.com"]. Checker: active gt true -> ERROR; emails co ... -> WARNING.

GET /ServiceProviderConfig (RFC 7644 section 4, RFC 7643 5). It returns patch.supported, bulk.supported (+ bulk.maxOperations, bulk.maxPayloadSize), filter.supported (+ filter.maxResults), changePassword.supported, sort.supported, etag.supported and authenticationSchemes. Also read /ResourceTypes (endpoints, schema extensions) and /Schemas (attributes the server really implements). Do not send features advertised as false: the server may return 501 or ignore them.

PATCH /Users/{id} with {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],"Operations":[{"op":"replace","path":"emails[type eq \"work\"].value","value":"b.jensen@example.com"}]}. The value filter selects only the work email and .value replaces just its address, leaving other emails and their type/primary untouched. No array indexes (emails[0] is invalid). If no work email exists, replace with a filter yields 400 noTarget; then use add on "emails" with [{"type":"work","value":"..."}]. Success: 200 with resource or 204. Checker: OK.

Yes. RFC 7643 section 4.2 prose says Group displayName is REQUIRED, while the machine-readable schema in 8.7 says required: false (reported erratum 5368, not verified); the prose wins, so always send displayName when creating a Group. It is a readWrite string, caseExact false, uniqueness none. Servers that copied the 8.7 schema may accept groups without it, so check the provider's /Schemas.

Give the earlier POST a bulkId (required for POST operations), and reference it later as "bulkId:<id>" anywhere a resource id is expected, e.g. op1 {"method":"POST","path":"/Users","bulkId":"qwerty","data":{...User...}} then op2 {"method":"POST","path":"/Groups","bulkId":"ytrewq","data":{"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Group"],"displayName":"Tour Guides","members":[{"type":"User","value":"bulkId:qwerty"}]}} (also usable in paths, e.g. /Users/bulkId:qwerty). The server substitutes the real id (RFC 7644 3.7.1/3.7.2) and must resolve or fail circular references. Bulk is optional (ServiceProviderConfig bulk.supported, maxOperations, maxPayloadSize; 413 if exceeded). Checker: OK.
